parsed.explanation: The traveller faces a genuine tier-1 universal exposure: this state bars gender-congruent restroom use in government-owned buildings and, from May 2026, in public colleges and universities, enforced by trespass with at least one documented arrest and 24-hour birth-sex custody. Layered on top is the national regime: passport X-marker elimination, discretionary refusal and possible (non-automatic) lifetime fraud findings, federal facility exclusion, documented abusive immigration and corrections custody, and counterterrorism rhetoric naming 'radically pro-transgender' groups. Offsetting: private commerce, hotels and transport are generally open; the federal hate-crime statute covers gender identity; courts work and have enjoined several orders; no documented police sweeps or organised targeting of trans visitors in this jurisdiction. Exposure is institutional and recurring, remedy partial — squarely the 0.35 tier, not 0.45.

entry_documents.exposure: National passport agency stopped issuing X markers; officers may refuse cases on sex discrepancy and consider lifetime fraud ineligibility (never automatic, all four elements required); trans athletes barred; secondary screening and pat-down outing risk at airports.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; visa fraud finding is discretionary, not automatic; litigation against the passport policy pending; legal-aid FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: A mismatched or X-marked home passport can move a traveller from screening into refused adjudication, and the encounter escalates within federal authority the state cannot constrain.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections model from 2026 imposes hair-cutting, hormone withdrawal and psychiatric substitution on trans inmates; immigration custody documents forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse of trans men; the 2025 restroom arrestee was held in a men's ward; this state runs a freeze-frame treatment restriction.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Federal gender-identity hate-crime statute; courts have enjoined several executive orders; local custody placement practice for trans detainees not documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A trespass or document-discrepancy arrest feeds into birth-sex placement and treatment-restricting custody, where the state's freeze-frame policy and federal practice compound.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State ban on gender-congruent facilities in government-owned buildings, expanded 15 May 2026 to public colleges and universities; national order bars federal single-sex facilities congruent with identity; trespass charge documented, held in men's ward.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Offence requires willful entry plus refusal to depart, not entry alone; private settings uncovered (this state is not among the six reaching private premises); an injunction protects one student plaintiff during litigation.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor entering a capitol, courthouse, public university or federal building is exposed by both layers; private hotels and shops are not, so exposure is setting-specific but recurring.

care_services.exposure: National orders frame minor gender-affirming care as mutilation; 27 states ban it; proposed national rules would bar public insurance reimbursement under 18; hospital records subpoenaed.
care_services.protection: No documented denial of emergency care or ward exclusion by birth sex for adult visitors in this jurisdiction; private clinics unmonitored either way.
care_services.interaction: Adult emergency care appears on ordinary terms; a travelling minor needing trans-related care encounters the federal and state prohibition directly.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; justice guidance lists 'radical gender ideology' among extremist animating viewpoints; teachers prosecuted for affirming trans minors.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Same documents state counterterrorism will not target mere disagreement; the reward memorandum does not use gender ideology as a criterion; no evidence of trans visitors investigated under it.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing raises the severity of any official encounter (protest, online speech, activism) but is not documented reaching ordinary tourists.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans students in this state's public schools and universities must use birth-sex restrooms; national order directs investigation and prosecution of teachers affirming a minor's transition; care bans for minors; subpoenas for under-19 records.
minors_guardians.protection: Facilities statute exempts chaperoning an accompanying child under 12; one student's injunction; several federal orders enjoined.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian accompanying a trans minor in public education or clinical settings faces both state facility law and federal prosecution/care exposure; private tourism settings are largely unaffected.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state hate-crime statute covering gender identity; sodomy provision unrepealed; 66% of polled residents back birth-sex document rules, signalling social friction to hostility; violence rate undocumented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime statute covers gender identity; police and courts function and have prosecuted bias cases federally; no documented organised targeting or police sweeps against trans visitors here.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Ordinary policing protects more than it threatens, but the absence of state bias-crime machinery leaves street hostility remedied only federally.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Facility-ban complaints have not produced relief; oversight findings on custody recur without change; passport policy remains in force pending suit.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts: injunctions against several executive orders, one facilities injunction protecting a plaintiff, legal-aid guidance available; federal civil-rights litigation ongoing.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies operate partially and slowly; they mitigate some federal overreach but do not displace the state facility rule or border practice.

anchor_checks.comparison: Very similar: a public-building birth-sex facility rule enforced against visitors, complaints rejected, no exemption on a foreign passport, polite private commerce. This jurisdiction adds a harsher border/document regime and documented custody-treatment restrictions, but lacks the anchor's blanket universal building scope and ward rule, and its courts do deliver some relief.

Below it: the 0.55-B profile has only localised service hostility with working readmission and compensation, no state facility ban. Here a statutory facility exclusion with a documented arrest plus federal document and custody exposure is a heavier, universal, state-imposed layer rather than patchy private conduct.

Far below: that profile combines a functioning remedy, ordinary courts granting relief, accepted documents and no facility exclusion. This jurisdiction has an unremedied statutory facility ban, tightening document rules at entry, and documented abusive custody, offset only by a working federal hate-crime statute.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is the sum of a hostile national document, screening, facility and custody apparatus and a state that legislates its own birth-sex facility rule and prison treatment freeze-frame. A visitor's private travel — hotels, shops, restaurants, transport — is largely open; the exposure bites at the border, in government and campus buildings, and above all if a document discrepancy or a facility complaint triggers detention, where custody practice is documented as harmful. Courts and the federal hate-crime statute are real but partial offsets, relieving some federal orders while leaving the state facility rule and passport practice operative.
